I'm Anthony Raborn, a psychometrician and statistician. I specialize in applied measurement, reproducible analytics, and custom R/Shiny decision tools.

My work combines psychometric methods, statistical programming, and practical software development to help organizations make clearer decisions from complex assessment and operational data. I try to build tools that are easy to repeat, explain, and use at any level of technical expertise.

I've been consulting off and on since graduate school, and I now do that work as Raborn Decision Sciences.

## Education

PhD in Research and Evaluation Methodology, Minor in Statistics

University of Florida | Gainesville, FL | May 2019

## Areas of expertise

- Psychometrics and assessment analytics
- Item analysis, DIF, equating, standard setting, and technical reporting
- R package development, deployment, and reproducible workflows
- Shiny dashboards and decision-support tools
- Quarto reports and technical documentation
- Operations and break-even modeling

## Selected publications

The first four describe the methods used in my R packages. The last is from my applied work on clinical trials. The full list is on [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8083-4739).

::: {.rds-cites}
Raborn & Leite (2018). [ShortForm: An R package to select scale short forms with the ant colony optimization algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1177/0146621617752993). *Applied Psychological Measurement*.

Raborn, Leite & Marcoulides (2020). [A comparison of metaheuristic optimization algorithms for scale short-form development](https://doi.org/10.1177/0013164420906600). *Educational and Psychological Measurement*.

Raborn & Sarı (2021). [Mixed adaptive multistage testing: A new approach](https://doi.org/10.21031/epod.871014). *Journal of Measurement and Evaluation in Education and Psychology*.

Huggins-Manley, Raborn, et al. (2024). [A nonparametric composite group DIF index for focal groups stemming from multicategorical variables](https://doi.org/10.1111/jedm.12394). *Journal of Educational Measurement*.

Raborn et al. (2025). [Psychometric analysis of the Neuro-QoL Fatigue in generalized myasthenia gravis using data from a phase 3 trial](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11136-025-03998-9). *Quality of Life Research*.
:::
